data.content_ref: inline:Counterexample to the most tempting expansion: resolving suspensions by bounded-depth lookahead and promoting UNDECIDED nodes. In the grounded extension a node is IN iff all its attackers are eventually OUT, so every UNDECIDED node has at least one attacker that is not OUT in the final labeling. Any promotion of such a node either adds nothing (all-attackers-OUT nodes are already IN) or changes the acceptance rule and can create conflict cycles — a promoted node whose attacker is also promoted — breaking determinism of the fixed point and reinstatement-as-derived. Negative result: the lever is the edge set, not the labeling rule; naive 'reinstatement acceleration' is a trap that must be refused.
